reason: The bone picture shows spaces for mineral, so strengthening the framework is a clear place to start.
expectation: I expect the mineral to fill the spaces and make the living bones better able to resist compression.

alternatives.reason: The front attachments also show where muscle cells belong, but I want to strengthen the bones first.

effect: The bones are strengthened while the joint remains movable; next I can build the muscles.
reaction: The contrast between hard bone and the still-movable joint makes sense.
reason: The front attachments show where muscle cells can go, so I'll start on that side of the elbow.
expectation: I expect the cells to form a muscle between the front tendons, though I'm not sure how the game will show it developing.

alternatives.reason: The back attachments also need muscle, but either side seems reasonable to start with.

effect: The front cells formed the biceps, which pulls to bend the elbow. The back attachments still need muscle.
reaction: The arrows made the link between the muscle's position and bending clear.
reason: The back attachments are the only remaining offered combination and need muscle to complete the opposite side.
expectation: I expect a muscle to form behind the elbow and pull the forearm in the opposite direction.

effect: The triceps completes the opposite side: its attachments make the same kind of pulling cells straighten rather than bend the elbow.
reaction: The comparison with the biceps made the role of attachment position clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building both muscles was most worthwhile because the arrows connected where each muscle pulls to how the elbow moves.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral was clear but less engaging than seeing the muscles produce opposite movements.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cells can help bend or straighten the elbow depending on their attachments.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless: the pictures showed spaces for mineral and cells, although the back muscle was the only remaining combination when I chose it.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see more connections between body structures and what they do, though the choices here were fairly straightforward.
